After the wedding, the two of them flew back home. The son went on a trip with the non-Jewish woman whom he was dating, making the father feel even more worried. Did this mean that they were becoming closer than before? Were they planning to get married soon?

He could barely sleep at night from worry. When the son came back from the trip, his father feared the worst. But to his complete shock, the son announced that his relationship had ended with that non-Jewish woman. They had nothing to do with each other anymore!

What a relief! Baruch Hashem, he wouldn’t marry a non-Jew after all! The father was so grateful to the Rebbe for his brachos.

Shortly afterward, someone thought of a Jewish woman who would be a perfect shidduch for the son. At the same time, another person thought of the exact same idea. They both called up the son to tell him about her, and the two began dating right away.

This was an incredible miracle. After four long years of dating a non-Jew, the son decided not to continue just a short time after visiting the Ohel! And, soon enough, he had begun dating a Jewish woman, making plans to build a Jewish home together.

As chassidim of the Rebbe, we know that we, too, can turn to the Rebbe when we face a challenge. Even if it seems impossible to overcome, the Rebbe is a big tzaddik who is above nature. He can make miracles happen!

His son had been dating a non- Jewish woman for four years. Was there any hope that he would marry a Yid?

Mazel tov! Our family friends from Brazil were making a wedding in Crown Heights, and we couldn’t wait to go to the chasunah. Mommy said we could even stay up late for dancing!

Many people flew in for the wedding, including a father and son who weren’t frum. But while all the other guests were in great moods and excited to join in the simcha, the father felt very down. As much as he tried to be happy, there was something weighing heavily on his heart that made him very sad.

You see, his son had been dating a non- Jewish woman for four years, and they would probably end up getting married.

he wasn’t frum, he knew how important it was for a Jew to marry someone Jewish. He had tried everything he could to convince his son not to marry her, but nothing helped.

As he thought about his son’s sad situation, he suddenly remembered the time he had seen the Rebbe before Gimmel Tammuz. You know what, he thought, instead of spending the day touring New York City, I’ll take my son to visit the Ohel. Surely the Rebbe will help!

His son, who had never been to the Ohel before, agreed to come along. They canceled their touring plans and Ubered all the way from Manhattan to Queens to visit the Ohel.

The two of them entered the Ohel and stood before the Rebbe. With tears in his eyes, the father began to daven: “Rebbe, please help my son end his relationship with this non- Jewish woman and find a Jewish wife!”

The father’s thoughts traveled back to his Bar Mitzvah many years ago, when he had received a personal letter from the Rebbe. continued: “Rebbe, I will start putting on tefillin again in

the merit that my son should marry someone Jewish.”
